title: Ines and the Vector
premise: Dominic Lockridge, a clone who inherited his original's unsolved murder case and a cargo hauler called the Vector, answers a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct for two centuries — and finds a dying woman named Ines who claims to be the original's killer. To keep two rival fleets from igniting a war over the signal's source, Dominic must sustain the fiction that the extinct civilization still lives, feeding both fleets fabricated transmissions while uncovering that his own murder was staged to bury the truth about the colony ship Meridian. When the deception collapses, Dominic chooses to expose the Meridian's fate — that its people became the 'extinct' language's last speakers — trading his inherited identity for a new one among the survivors. The war dissolves into negotiation, and Dominic, finally free of Lockridge's ghost, stays with Ines and her found family aboard the Vector.
about_author: Ines Yarrow is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who wrote her first novel during long shifts monitoring contested shipping lanes. She lives in a coastal city with too many houseplants and a stubborn belief that found families make better stories than bloodlines.

chapters.title: Dead Language, Live Signal
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Hauling freight through contested orbits, Dominic intercepts a distress call in a language dead for two centuries. His ship AI flags it as impossible; his creditors flag him as delinquent. He should ignore it. Instead he burns fuel he doesn't have toward the source. Emotional beat: restless curiosity overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Airlock
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He finds a crippled survey skiff and rescues Ines Voss, half-frozen and lying fluently about who she is. She recognizes his face instantly — and calls him by his original's name before he introduces himself. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, flashback-laced. Ines admits she knew the first Dominic Lockridge — the man whose murder case Dominic inherited unresolved three years ago. She claims innocence but knows details never made public. Emotional beat: the past pressing on the present like a hand on the throat.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She reveals the distress signal will draw both the Concord fleet and the Rimward Compact to the same coordinates within weeks. Her plan: fabricate ongoing transmissions from the 'lost civilization' so each side believes the other is negotiating exclusively. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership forged out of mutual blackmail potential.

chapters.title: Vector Math
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They retrofit the Vector's comms array to synthesize the dead language using fragments Ines memorized. First forged transmission goes out; a Concord picket alters course. It's working. Emotional beat: grim exhilaration of getting away with it.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She confesses she was the Meridian colony ship's archivist, one of the last speakers of its language, and that the original Lockridge was investigating the Meridian's disappearance when he died. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through professional detachment.

chapters.title: Cargo of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine delivery becomes a trap when a Compact officer boards and questions Dominic about anomalous signals traced near his route. He lies well — too well, he realizes, like a man rehearsed. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming.

chapters.title: The Murder File
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Digging into his inherited case files, Dominic finds evidence his original's death was staged: no body recovered, life insurance routed to an anonymous trust. Someone wanted Lockridge erased, not killed. Emotional beat: vertigo of doubting your own origin.

chapters.title: Concord at the Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A Concord delegation requests parley with the 'civilization' aboard the Vector. Ines performs first contact alone while Dominic hides, improvising ritual phrases from memory. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into strange, intoxicating authority.

chapters.title: Compact Interference
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Compact cracks the forgery's timing patterns and sends an ultimatum: produce the aliens or be declared hostile. The lie now has a countdown. Emotional beat: the price of survival becoming literal.

chapters.title: Meridian Wreck
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Following Ines's archival coordinates, they find the Meridian itself — not destroyed, but scuttled deliberately, its crew scattered as refugees by a Concord cover-up decades ago. Emotional beat: righteous fury and vindication entwined.

chapters.title: The Survivors
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They locate a hidden settlement of Meridian descendants who abandoned their language to hide. Some remember Ines; none forgive her silence. Emotional beat: homecoming that feels like exile.

chapters.title: Family of Strangers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. While Ines negotiates with the wary settlers, Dominic fixes their failing water recyclers and is slowly folded into their routines — meals, arguments, a child teaching him card games. Emotional beat: found family arriving unannounced.

chapters.title: Blackmail and Bargains
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A Concord intelligence officer, Sera Iqbal, confronts Ines privately: she knows the transmissions are fake, and offers to keep the secret in exchange for the Meridian evidence — to use against her own admiralty. Emotional beat: trust extended across enemy lines, cautiously.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Both fleets converge on the Vector's position with weapons hot, each believing the other has seized the aliens. The lie can hold maybe forty more hours. Emotional beat: claustrophobic inevitability.

chapters.title: The Original Returns
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The first Dominic Lockridge steps off a Concord shuttle — alive, complicit in staging his own death, and the man who buried the Meridian report under orders. He demands Ines's silence and offers Dominic his old life back. Emotional beat: identity as a cage offered like a gift.

chapters.title: Confession at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Lockridge reveals Ines didn't kill him — she helped fake it to protect the Meridian survivors, then spent years paying for it. But he'll let the fleets destroy the settlement rather than be exposed. Emotional beat: betrayal inside alliance, love inside betrayal.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Climax begins: Dominic hijacks the Vector's array and broadcasts the truth in every language aboard — the Meridian's real history, Lockridge's staged death, the cover-up — to both fleets simultaneously. Emotional beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Wreck
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Fleets hold fire as the broadcast spreads through their crews; sailors with Meridian ancestry mutiny quietly, refusing the order to shoot. Lockridge attempts to destroy the wreck and is stopped — by Dominic, physically, at last facing his original. Emotional beat: the climax's held breath.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Lockridge is arrested by his own fleet; Iqbal testifies; negotiations open between Concord and Compact with the Meridian survivors at the table — speaking their language openly for the first time in decades. Emotional beat: weary, hard-won justice.

chapters.title: What Dominic Keeps
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Offered reinstatement, a name cleared, a life restored, Dominic declines. He signs the Vector over to himself — legally, this time — and asks the settlers if there's room for one more at dinner. Emotional beat: choosing the present over the inherited past.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing chapter. Weeks later, the Vector carries Meridian families to a new charter under joint protection. Ines teaches Dominic the language's first words; a child corrects his accent mercilessly. The signal they answer now is simply someone calling home. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
